plainFields.description: [Actor type] - Who performed this action ('system', 'administrator'). Distinct from user IDs for flexible audit classification.

plainFields.name: decision_state
plainFields.description: [Decision state] - status after action (pending, approved, rejected, escalated). Used for compliance/state tracking. No redundant aggregates.

plainFields.name: reason_detail
plainFields.description: [Reason detail] - Optional field for detailed rationale/context for decisions. Null if no further explanation (atomic, not denormalized).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created at] - Timestamp for log creation. Implements full change log, normalized per row.

plainIndexes.description: Index for fast audit lookups of workflow steps by seller.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_seller_verification_document
models.description:
[Seller Verification Document Model] - This implements the verification, compliance, and audit traceability requirement from Seller/Admin Management. 

Captures all official/verifiable documents (business registration, tax certificates, etc) that are submitted by a seller during/after onboarding. Each record represents a single document. Maintains 3NF through separation of document meta from business profile.

Key relationships: Links to seller, business profile. Referenced by admin log for moderation. 
Special behaviors: Each represents a single document, soft deletable but used in audits (removed only if legally allowed).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique ID for verification document row (implements atomic document record). Normalized to ensure traceable compliance entries.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: [Seller linkage] - Links to ai_ecommerce_seller for ownership of each submitted document. Follows foreign key pattern for separation, normalized for each seller.

foreignFields.name: business_profile_id
foreignFields.description: [Business Profile linkage] - References ai_ecommerce_seller_business_profile for relationship to business meta. Normalized for 3NF compliance.

plainFields.name: document_type
plainFields.description: [Document type] - (e.g. 'business_registration', 'tax_certificate', etc). Implements requirement for atomic document categorization without denormalization.

plainFields.name: document_file_url
plainFields.description: [Document file URL] - Points to uploaded/document archive (S3/etc). Ensures atomicity of file linkage under 3NF.

plainFields.name: issue_date
plainFields.description: [Document issue date] - Date document was issued (for expiry/validity checks). Atomic datetime for normalized schema.

plainFields.name: expiry_date
plainFields.description: [Document expiry date] - Optional. Date document becomes invalid/obsolete. Null if not applicable. 3NF atomic field.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: [Verified at] - Timestamp when document was verified by admin/staff. Null if not yet verified. Normalized per row.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: [Deleted at] - Soft deletion timestamp for audit log. Null if active. Normalized for 3NF and auditability.

plainIndexes.description: Document type per seller for quick lookup/filter in audit workflows.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_admin_action_log
models.description:
[Administrator Action Log Model] - This model implements action and incident tracking for compliance as described in the requirements: captures all sensitive or policy-changing actions performed by administrators for full audit and traceability.

Each log row represents a unique admin action (role/config changes, onboarding, data export, system override, etc) with normalized links to actor and related entities. Ensures normalization by avoiding data duplication; information is split into log, actor/admin, and affected target(s).

Key relationships: Links to administrator, seller (if action is seller-centric), or customer/user (if needed).
Special behaviors: Immutable, append-only; used in compliance audits and regulatory checks.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique admin action log ID. Implements atomic key for incident/compliance audit, required for normalized structure.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: [Administrator linkage] - References ai_ecommerce_administrator (who performed the action). Required for actor tracing and compliance. Maintains normalized audit structure.

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description: [Role linkage] - Optionally ties this admin action to a role event or policy change if the action is related. Maintains 3NF; nullable if not policy-related.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: [Seller linkage] - Optional reference to related seller if the action concerns a seller/company. Null if action is unrelated. Maintains normalized foreign reference.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: [Target type] - String describing the main subject of the admin action (e.g., 'user', 'seller', 'system_policy'). Implements normalized target specificity for logs.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: [Target ID] - Optional. Identifies the specific record/target affected by the action (if applicable). Null if non-record event. Maintains 3NF separation from admin log.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: [Action type] - Describes the action performed (e.g. 'role_grant', 'onboarding_approve', 'data_export'). Normalized atomic action descriptor.

plainFields.name: action_detail
plainFields.description: [Action detail] - Optional additional details/context about the action. Allows compliance depth, null if not required for simple actions. Normalized per log row.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created at] - Timestamp of when the admin action/access occurred. 3NF-compliant atomic timestamp, never pre-aggregated.

plainIndexes.description: For fast audit trail/review by admin's activity timeline.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_role
models.description:
[Role Model] - Implements structured RBAC requirement from Seller/Admin specification. 

Represents a single logical role (e.g., 'seller', 'admin', 'product_manager', 'auditor') used by users/administrators for permission mapping and access control. Maintains strict normalization by decoupling roles from users/actors and grouping only role descriptions (no permissions/assignments included directly).

Key relationships: Used by permissions model(s), and assignment to actors (users, sellers, admins).
Special behaviors: Cannot be deleted while assigned to any actor; role name is globally unique.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique ID for each role (atomic, normalized structure). Required for mapping roles to permissions/actors.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: [Role name] - Implements RBAC naming. E.g., 'administrator', 'seller', etc. Atomic per role.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Description] - Free-text business purpose of this role. Used for UI/help compliance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created at] - Timestamp for role creation. Ensures audit of role lifecycle.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Updated at] - Timestamp for last modification. Maintains normalized, atomic history.

uniqueIndexes.description: Globally unique index on role name, as only one role of each kind should exist.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_permission
models.description:
[Permission Model] - Implements structured, fine-grained permission system in support of RBAC (see requirements on privilege separation and fine-grained control).

Represents a single application-level permission that can be linked to one or more roles. Each permission record captures the unique, atomic concept of an allowed action/resource (e.g., 'manage_orders', 'approve_seller', 'export_data'). Strict 3NF compliance: this table does not map to users or roles directly, but only describes the permission concept.

Key relationships: Linked from joining table(s) (not present here) for mapping of which roles have which permissions. Used in all access-control checks.
Special behaviors: Permission name is unique; cannot be deleted while assigned to any role.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique permission ID (atomic, for linkage by roles or audit).

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: [Permission name] - Implements atomic permission string (e.g. 'manage_orders'). Globally unique for enforcement.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Description] - Free-text summary of permission. For audit and documentation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created at] - Creation time of permission. For audit/history.

uniqueIndexes.description: Globally unique index for permission name. Avoid conflict in RBAC mapping.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_products
models.description:
[Product Entity] - This implements the product definition, catalog management, and onboarding requirement as analyzed from the Product Management, System Overview, and Business Concepts requirement documents.

Defines the core sellable item in the platform, referenced by SKUs, categories, and media. Maintains strict 3NF: all descriptive and variant fields are separated into related tables (options, tags, media, inventory). This structure enables scalable product onboarding, flexible catalog relationships, and AI-driven enrichment.

For example, a seller can create a product with multilingual title/description, assign to multiple categories, upload rich media, and manage compliance status.

Key relationships: owned by a seller, has many SKUs, belongs to many categories (M:N), references options, media, tags.
Special behaviors: Approval and compliance workflow states are enforced; no denormalization (aggregates in MVs only).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique platform identifier for the product. Implements global uniqueness with UUID as required by architecture and compliance requirements. Enables strict 3NF and referencing from all related entities (SKUs, categories, media, etc.).

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: [Seller Relationship] - Links product to the seller owner. Required for RBAC and enforcement of seller-specific permissions, as per Seller/Admin Management requirements. Ensures strict foreign-key normalization. Every product must have a seller owner with referential integrity to ai_ecommerce_sellers.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: [Product Title] - Product display name (multilingual via related media if needed). Implements requirements for rich, flexible product names. Strictly atomic field. Example: 'AI-Enabled Smart Vacuum'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Product Description] - Detailed description (long text, normalized but atomic; multilingual handled in media/options). Enables AI-enriched copy, templates. Example: 'Next-gen AI-powered vacuum with voice assistant integration.'

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: [Product Lifecycle Status] - Implements catalog workflow state (e.g., draft, pending, published, archived). Enforces catalog management lifecycle (3NF: workflow states and timestamps atomic). Example: 'published'.

plainFields.name: approval_state
plainFields.description: [Product Approval State] - Captures compliance/approval state per requirements. Linked to audit but atomic here. Example: 'approved'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - Automatic record creation, atomic timestamp for auditing. Fulfills audit trail requirements. Example: '2025-01-01T12:00:00Z'.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Updated Timestamp] - Last modified timestamp; supports audit logs and automation (atomic). Fulfills audit trail and version tracking requirements.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: [Soft Delete] - Implements data retention and deletion compliance (nullable). Null if not deleted, otherwise soft-deleted for GDPR/KISA retention.

uniqueIndexes.name: unique_product_title_per_seller
uniqueIndexes.description: Prevents duplicate product names for the same seller, upholding business uniqueness constraint.

plainIndexes.name: idx_product_status_approval
plainIndexes.description: Enables filter/search by catalog/workflow state in product management and admin approval pipelines.

ginIndexes.name: gin_idx_product_title
ginIndexes.description: Full-text fuzzy search for product names (enables AI/UX-driven suggestions and typo tolerance).

models.name: ai_ecommerce_skus
models.description:
[SKU Entity] - This implements normalized stock-keeping unit granularity for each product variation (size, color, etc.), reflecting the Product Management and Inventory requirements. 

Each SKU represents a unique sellable product configuration, managed atomically. Linked to products, inventory, and optionally to product options (e.g., color, size).

For example, SKUs allow separate price, barcode, and inventory per variant; a T-shirt product could have several SKUs for each combination of size/color.

Key relationships: Links to product, inventory, and option tables. 3NF: All computed inventory/price is materialized only in MV tables.
Special behaviors: Uniqueness enforced per product and variant details.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique identifier for the SKU. Required for unambiguous SKU-level operations and auditing, per inventory/fulfillment requirements.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: [Product Foreign Key] - Denotes which product this SKU belongs to. Enforces referential integrity to ai_ecommerce_products, normalized 1:N product/SKU relationship.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: [SKU Code] - System/barcode, unique within product. For business operations and integrations, 3NF atomic field. Example: 'SKU-121212-BLK-S'.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: [SKU Price] - Normalized unit price. Maintains price atomicity, no computed totals. Example: 129.99.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: [Currency Code] - ISO 4217 code. Required for multicurrency; atomic (3NF). Example: 'KRW' or 'USD'.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: [Active Flag] - True if this SKU is available for purchase, false otherwise. Implements lifecycle rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [SKU Created At] - Audit/timestamp. Required for 3NF, enables full traceability.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [SKU Updated At] - Last modified timestamp; atomic for temporal consistency.

uniqueIndexes.name: unique_sku_code_per_product
uniqueIndexes.description: SKU codes must be unique within each product context (business and system constraint).

plainIndexes.name: idx_sku_active_price
plainIndexes.description: Enables efficient inventory/price filtering in operational APIs.

ginIndexes.name: gin_idx_sku_code
ginIndexes.description: GIN-powered partial search for SKU code, supporting integrations and bulk ops.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_categories
models.description:
[Category Entity] - Implements product category taxonomy and assignment per Product Management requirements.

Categories organize products into hierarchies (1:N, optional parent), enabling dynamic navigation, filtering, and AI-powered merchandising.

Example: Electronics, sub-category: AI Gadgets.

Normalization: Each category is atomic; M:N with products is managed by join table (not shown here for focus). Parent/child handled via parent_id FK (self-referencing).

Key relationships: Products (M:N via join or denormalized in MVs), self-reference for hierarchy, referenced by options/media.
Special behaviors: Category path/ordering determined by app logic, not by pre-calculated fields.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique ID for every category. Required for taxonomy operations/support.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: [Parent Category FK] - Enables recursive category structure (optional, nullable). 3NF: avoids denormalization.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: [Category Name] - Atomic display name. Example: 'AI Home Robots'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Description] - Category details; used for navigation/help, atomic, not aggregated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - Category creation, for auditing and navigation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Updated Timestamp] - Last modified timestamp, for change audits.

uniqueIndexes.name: unique_category_name_per_parent
uniqueIndexes.description: Enforces no duplicate sibling categories by name under a parent.

plainIndexes.name: idx_category_created_at
plainIndexes.description: Operational usage for recency sort/filter.

ginIndexes.name: gin_idx_category_name
ginIndexes.description: Full-text partial search for category navigation/AI suggestions.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_inventories
models.description:
[Inventory Entity] - Implements per-SKU, per-location inventory tracking, as required in Product Management and Cart/Order System requirements.

Every inventory record is atomic: unique per SKU+location; no pre-calculated totals. Enables real-time inventory audit, tracked movements (snapshots/audit not shown here).

Example: SKU at warehouse 'Seoul #1' has 100 available units.

Key relationships: 1:N from SKU, location reference (string for normalization; multi-location in app logic).
Special behaviors: Audit traceability ensured by atomic fields and no aggregations.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique per inventory record. Reference for all inventory operations.

foreignFields.name: sku_id
foreignFields.description: [SKU FK] - Inventory is tracked for a specific SKU. Enforces strict referential integrity (app-level multi-location enabled).

plainFields.name: location
plainFields.description: [Location Name] - Normalized, atomic warehouse or fulfillment location. Example: 'KR-Seoul-001'.

plainFields.name: quantity_available
plainFields.description: [Current Available Quantity] - Non-aggregated count, always atomic per record. No pre-calculated totals allow full normalization. Example: 50.

plainFields.name: quantity_reserved
plainFields.description: [Reserved Quantity] - Quantity reserved (e.g., in open orders), atomic only for current status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Inventory Created Timestamp] - For audit trace. Enables temporal queries.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Inventory Updated Timestamp] - Per-transaction stock change tracking.

uniqueIndexes.name: unique_inventory_per_sku_location
uniqueIndexes.description: Prevents same SKU+location combo duplications. One record per unique SKU/location.

plainIndexes.name: idx_inventory_location
plainIndexes.description: Fast lookup per warehouse/location.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_media
models.description:
[Media Entity] - Manages product/SKU/category-attached files and media (images, video, etc.), implementing requirements for rich multimedia and multilingual support from Product Management and System Overview.

Each attachment is atomic: URL, type, and owner entity type; strictly normalized.

Example: A product with 4 image URLs for different languages/views.

Key relationships: Linked to product, SKU, or category, 1:N to any owner via discriminated owner_type + owner_id.
Special behaviors: No denormalization; full localization handled by content fields where needed.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Each media asset has a globally unique ID, for robust referencing.

foreignFields.name: owner_id
foreignFields.description: [Owner FK] - Points to ai_ecommerce_products.id, ai_ecommerce_skus.id, or ai_ecommerce_categories.id depending on owner_type.

plainFields.name: owner_type
plainFields.description: [Owner Type] - Discriminator for product, sku, or category. Only one allowed per row.

plainFields.name: uri
plainFields.description: [Media URI] - Where the file is stored (CDN, S3, etc.). Business compliance: strictly atomic, never concatenated/aggregate field.

plainFields.name: media_type
plainFields.description: [Media Type] - File type (image, video, etc.), atomic field for safe rendering. Example: 'image/png'.

plainFields.name: language
plainFields.description: [Language Code] - Optional, ISO format for localization (e.g., 'en','ko').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - Audit/item lifecycle field.

uniqueIndexes.name: unique_media_owner_uri
uniqueIndexes.description: Prevents duplicate media per asset per entity.

plainIndexes.name: idx_media_owner_type
plainIndexes.description: Quick lookup for different media relationships.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_product_options
models.description:
[Product Option Entity] - Implements normalized, atomic representation of selectable product options (e.g., color, size), according to Product Management and personalization requirements.

Allows dynamic, AI-powered option structures. Each record is atomic (no array fields, one row per product/option name/value pair).

Example: One record for 'Color/Red', another for 'Size/Large' for the same product.

Key relationships: Linked to product and (optionally) SKU, enforcing 3NF. Integrates with AI model/materialized views for ML-powered variant suggestion.
Special behaviors: Designed for maximum flexibility in personalization workflows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique identifier for the option row.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: [Product FK] - Each option points to the owning product. Strict referential integrity, no nullable references.

foreignFields.name: sku_id
foreignFields.description: [SKU FK] - Option may be further scoped to a specific SKU (nullable if generic option).

plainFields.name: option_name
plainFields.description: [Option Name] - e.g., 'color', 'size', atomic field. Used for AI-driven variant personalization.

plainFields.name: option_value
plainFields.description: [Option Value] - Selected value for this option (e.g., 'red', 'XL'), strictly atomic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - Option audit record (atomic, for option version tracking).

uniqueIndexes.name: unique_option_per_product_sku
uniqueIndexes.description: Enforces 3NF for option assignments, prevents duplications across SKUs.

plainIndexes.name: idx_option_name
plainIndexes.description: For filtering/suggestion/AI analytics on distinct option types.

ginIndexes.name: gin_idx_option_value
ginIndexes.description: Flexible, typo-tolerant AI-driven search/filter for option values.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_product_compliance_rules
models.description:
[Product Compliance Rule Entity] - Implements explicit, normalized catalog for compliance rules that products must meet, per architecture and compliance requirements.

Each record defines an atomic compliance criterion (e.g., safety approval, age limit, localization), referenced by products for state enforcement.

Key relationships: Many-to-Many (implemented via join elsewhere). Each rule is atomic, managed independently for compliance upgrades/future law changes.

Example: Rule 'KFDA Safety' applies to multiple products, and a product may require passing several rules.

3NF: Purely atomic rule definition, no pre-applied aggregates/state per product here.
Special behaviors: Approval state for each product/rule is handled in join (elsewhere).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique atomic rule identifier.

plainFields.name: rule_name
plainFields.description: [Rule Name] - Canonical, atomic rule label. Example: 'No Sale Under 18'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Rule Description] - Explanation/details for this rule. Strictly normalized atomic text (no aggregation).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - For audit/compliance recordkeeping.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_product_tags
models.description:
[Product Tag Entity] - Implements atomic tag definition, strictly normalized per AI/product management guidelines. Enables flexible, user-defined and AI-generated tagging systems, referenced by products and MVs for search/recommendation.

For example, 'AI', 'Smart Home', or 'Eco-friendly' tag records, linked in M:N elsewhere. Pure 3NF: Tag state per product (assigned_by, date) is joined in mapping table, not here.

Key relationships: Many-to-many to products; referenced in analytics and personalization modules (cross-file integrity).
Special behaviors: Tag lifecycle managed separately from assignment/analytics.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique tag ID, used platform-wide in tagging.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: [Tag Name] - Atomic tag text, unique by business rule (per requirements). Example: 'AI', 'Smart Home'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - Tag lifecycle atomic timestamp.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_product
models.description:
[Product Entity] - Implements the unified product definition and catalog management requirement from Product Management, System Overview, and Business Concepts documents. 

Defines the core sellable concept in the ecommerce platform. Strictly 3NF: all descriptive fields, variations, options, tags, and attachments are atomic or fully normalized in related tables. Enables scalable onboarding, flexible categorization (joins elsewhere), and compliance automation.

Example: A seller creates a product with title/description, assigns categories, uploads media, and is subject to approval flow. 

Key relationships: Owned by {\@link ai_ecommerce_seller}, 1:N to SKUs, options, media, tags, and compliance join models. 
Special behaviors: Lifecycle/approval states are enforced, full auditability through created/updated/deleted timestamps. All aggregates appear in MVs only.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique global product ID for systemwide referencing, auditing, and relational integrity. Required for strict 3NF and cross-reference by SKUs, inventory, categories, etc.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: [Seller FK] - References owning seller ({\@link ai_ecommerce_seller}), enforcing seller-level product boundary and RBAC per Admin/Seller Management requirements. Non-null, normalized FK.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: [Product Title] - Human-friendly product display name. Multi-language via media. Strictly atomic per normalization. Example: 'AI Smart Watch'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Product Description] - Rich, atomic product details. Multilingual/content fields go to attachments. Example: 'Next-gen AI watch with health tracking.'

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: [Catalog Status] - Supports admin-seller workflow. Enum: draft, pending, published, archived. 3NF, atomic state transition only.

plainFields.name: approval_state
plainFields.description: [Approval State] - Tracks product verification/compliance state per auditing. Enum: pending, approved, rejected. 3NF, atomic state only.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - Auditing, entity creation. Required for full traceability.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Updated Timestamp] - Auditing, updated entity. Normalized per 3NF.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: [Soft Delete At] - Nullable for soft deletion/retention. Null if active, timestamp if deleted (for GDPR, compliance).

uniqueIndexes.name: uniq_product_title_seller
uniqueIndexes.description: Prevents duplicate product titles for the same seller per business and regulatory requirement.

plainIndexes.name: idx_product_status_approval
plainIndexes.description: Enables multi-state admin/seller catalog filtering and workflow management.

ginIndexes.name: gin_idx_product_title
ginIndexes.description: Supports full-text typo-tolerant product search and AI-driven name discovery.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_sku
models.description:
[SKU Entity] - Defines atomic stock-keeping units for each product configuration (per Product Management, Inventory, and Fulfillment requirements).

Each SKU represents a unique combination of options for purchase, price, and fulfillment tracking. Enforces full normalization: price, code, and state are separate from aggregate logic (such as stock or sales count, which are in MVs).

Example: For a T-shirt, SKUs for sizes S/M/L and colors Red/Blue.

Key relationships: Each SKU belongs to one product (FK), referenced by options and inventory. 
Special behaviors: Strict business uniqueness per (code,product), activation ensures SKU sale state.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique SKU record ID, required for transaction integrity and audit logging by Stock/Order systems.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: [Product FK] - SKU parent reference. Enforces unambiguous link to {\@link ai_ecommerce_product}. Required and normalized.

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: [SKU Code] - Barcode or logical SKU identifier. Unique per (product_id), 3NF, atomic. Example: 'T12345-RD-M'.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: [Unit Price] - Normalized single price for SKU. No calculated/discounted/total fields (handled elsewhere). Example: 199.0.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: [Currency] - ISO 4217 code enforced for transactional accuracy. Example: 'USD'.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: [Active] - Whether the SKU is for sale. Used in admin, seller, and order APIs for filtering. True = orderable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [SKU Created At] - Auditing and temporal queries for inventory and sales.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [SKU Updated At] - Record update/audit trail.

uniqueIndexes.name: uniq_sku_code_per_product
uniqueIndexes.description: Enforces catalogue uniqueness: each SKU code must be unique for the same product.

plainIndexes.name: idx_sku_is_active
plainIndexes.description: Accelerates inventory and catalogue filtering: list active/inactive SKUs.

ginIndexes.name: gin_idx_sku_code
ginIndexes.description: Full-text search on SKU code, enables bulk and integration lookups.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_category
models.description:
[Category Entity] - Implements multi-level product categorization as required by Product Management.

Each category is atomic; parent-child tree structure enforced via self-referencing parent_id. 3NF: all hierarchy and display information separated, no aggregates. M:N product mapping handled in separate join table (not here).

Example: Electronics > Wearables > Watches.

Key relationships: Self-referential parent_id, atomic name/description.
Special behaviors: Sibling uniqueness per parent enforced; app-level navigation/hierarchy handled in API.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Globally unique category ID for all taxonomy and navigation lookups.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: [Parent Category FK] - Nullable; allows for nested taxonomies. Null for root, otherwise recurses to id. 3NF: atomic relation only.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: [Category Name] - Display-friendly display name, unique under parent. Example: 'Electronics'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Category Description] - Human-friendly category context. No pre-aggregated content. Example: 'Smart devices and accessories.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - When category entered system. Required for queries/audit.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Updated Timestamp] - Track changes for audit/API navigation.

uniqueIndexes.name: uniq_category_name_parent
uniqueIndexes.description: Enforces prohibition on duplicate sibling categories by name under the same parent (key UX/business constraint).

plainIndexes.name: idx_category_created_at

models.name: ai_ecommerce_cart
models.description:
[Cart Purpose] - This implements the persistent shopping cart requirement from the AI E-Commerce Cart & Order System document.

A cart represents a customer's temporary, device/platform-synchronized collection of products intended for purchase, maintained before checkout. Maintains 3NF compliance by isolating temporary cart state from finalized order records, and by referencing only user and item entities via foreign keys. For example, customers can add, update, or remove products in their carts on mobile or web, retrieve cart items on login, and merge guest carts.

Key relationships: References customer (ai_ecommerce_customer), contains many ai_ecommerce_cart_items. Does not duplicate order data. Special behaviors: Ensures each customer has multiple carts (for different sessions), with soft-delete support and device context.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description:
[Primary Key] - Implements unique cart identity per instance.

Business meaning: Uniquely identifies a cart in the system, regardless of customer, device, or session. Ensures normalization by preventing duplication or ambiguity. For example, required in all cart CRUD queries and foreign key references. Cannot be null, auto-generated.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description:
[Customer Foreign Key] - Implements association to cart owner.

Business meaning: Links this cart to the owning customer profile. Ensures normalization by storing only the reference, avoiding duplication of customer info. For example, used to fetch all carts or recovered sessions for a given user. Cannot be null.

plainFields.name: device_context
plainFields.description:
[Device Context] - Implements device/session-specific state requirement.

Stores info like device type, browser fingerprint, or guest/registered status. Ensures normalization by not repeating device details in related records. For example, tracks whether cart originated from mobile app or guest session.

plainFields.name: cart_status
plainFields.description:
[Cart Status] - Implements cart state transitions (e.g., active, merged, expired) required for recovery and audit.

Normalized atomic state. For example, helps determine whether to merge, expire, or keep a cart open.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
[Created At] - Implements auditing and recovery.

Timestamp of cart creation. Ensures accurate recovery from session failures. Used for order of operation queries.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
[Updated At] - Tracks last modification, for expiration and merge logic.

Example: Auto-merge or expire if not updated recently.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
[Soft Delete] - Implements GDPR-compliant cart removal and temporary hide behavior.

Null if visible, datetime if soft-deleted. Ensures only logically deleted carts are hidden, data retained for compliance/audit.

uniqueIndexes.name: unique_cart_customer_device
uniqueIndexes.description: Enforces one cart per customer per device/session context, preventing duplicates. For example, cannot create two carts for same user/session.

plainIndexes.name: idx_cart_status_created_at
plainIndexes.description: Speeds queries for active/expired carts, supports cleanup jobs and recovery flows.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_cart_item
models.description:
[Cart Item Purpose] - Implements the requirement for per-item cart composition, enabling normalized tracking of which SKUs (products) and their quantities are held in a given cart at any time.

Business explanation: Each row represents a product (SKU) intended for purchase in the user's cart, with atomic quantity, added/modified timestamps. Maintains 3NF compliance by storing only SKU and quantity (no derived prices or product denormalization) and referencing the parent cart and SKU.

Key relationships: Linked to ai_ecommerce_cart and ai_ecommerce_sku. Special behaviors: Cannot store pre-calculated prices; quantity can be changed, and items removed/added per business logic.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Uniquely identifies this cart item row for precise updates/removal. For example, used when updating quantity or removing an item.

foreignFields.name: cart_id
foreignFields.description: [Cart FK] - Links item to its parent cart. Ensures normalization, enabling easy updates.

foreignFields.name: sku_id
foreignFields.description: [SKU FK] - Identifies the specific product/variation this item refers to. Necessary for managing product catalog changes. 3NF compliance ensured by referencing SKU only.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: [Item Quantity] - Number of units of this SKU in the cart. No calculation, only atomic value. Zero or more, depending on UX. Example: Increase to 3 for a bulk buy.

plainFields.name: added_at
plainFields.description: [Added At Timestamp] - Tracks when this SKU was added to cart for auditing, UI sort order.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Updated At Timestamp] - Maintains when quantity or SKU was last changed for this row. Example: Used in inventory holds or cart cleanup.

uniqueIndexes.name: unique_cart_item_per_sku

Represents a user purchase resulting from finalizing a cart, with references to customer, cart, payment, shipping info, and order status. Enforces 3NF by storing only atomic order data and keys; all calculations occur at business logic or in views. For example, used to audit, track, cancel, or return orders at every lifecycle phase.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_payment
models.description:
[Payment Purpose] - Centralizes payment transaction records for each order or wallet action, as required in the payment integration and discount/loyalty requirements.

Each payment row records a single payment event, including amount, provider, method, reference, and status. No pre-computed or aggregated fields. Maintains strict normalization and auditability.

Key relationships: Optionally links to ai_ecommerce_order, with amount/method fields; can also be tied to wallet transactions in broader schema. Special behaviors: Supports refunds, cancellations, multiple providers.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Payment PK] - Uniquely identifies a payment for audit, refund, or reconciliation.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: [Transaction Amount] - Atomic payment amount for audit. No total, no calculations here.

plainFields.name: provider
plainFields.description: [Payment Provider] - Payment integration reference string (e.g., 'stripe', 'toss', 'paypal'). No calcs or external duplication.

plainFields.name: method
plainFields.description: [Method] - The actual payment channel used (e.g., credit_card, bank_transfer). For analytics only.

plainFields.name: payment_reference
plainFields.description: [Provider Reference] - External processor ID if available. Null if not provided.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: [Status] - Payment state at this event (pending, completed, failed, cancelled, etc.). Enables reattempts, dispute management.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - For traceability and compliance.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Updated Timestamp] - For refunds, disputes, and reconciliation flows.

uniqueIndexes.name: unique_payment_reference
uniqueIndexes.description: Enforces one payment record per external provider reference, if provider issues unique reference.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_order_status_log
models.description:
[Order Status Log Purpose] - Implements an immutable, additive audit trail of all order status changes, supporting regulatory/compliance requirements for e-commerce platforms.

Each record represents a single status transition for an order (e.g., 'pending' → 'paid'), with actor, actor type, and timestamp. All audit logic is separated from live order data, enforcing strict normalization and minimizing update anomalies.

Key relationships: ai_ecommerce_order FK (target order); actor_id with actor_type supports references to customer, seller, or administrator (for multi-actor flows). Special behaviors: Appends only; never updated after creation.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Status Log PK] - Uniquely identifies this log for each state change entry.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: [Order FK] - Order being changed.

plainFields.name: old_status
plainFields.description: [Old Status] - Previous order status for change tracking, e.g., 'pending'.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: [New Status] - New status after transition.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: [Actor ID] - Who made the change (references customer, seller, admin based on context; polymorphic pattern).

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: [Actor Type] - Role of the actor: 'customer', 'seller', 'administrator'. Analytical/trace purpose only.

plainFields.name: changed_at
plainFields.description: [Changed At] - Transition timestamp, for legal/audit trail.

plainIndexes.name: idx_status_log_order_changed
plainIndexes.description: Optimizes order status log queries by order and chronology.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_shipment
models.description:
[Shipment Purpose] - Tracks outbound shipment details for each order, as required for fulfillment and delivery audit.

A shipment record is created per order, containing external tracking, carrier, and shipping status, not duplicating item, customer, or pricing data. Maintains 3NF compliance.

Key relationships: Order FK, optional carrier/provider string. Special behaviors: Supports multi-stage tracking and addresses, without denormalization of totals.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Shipment PK] - Unique shipment tracking for audit, return, status sync.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: [FK to Order] - Links shipment to its order. 1:1 mapping at regular e-commerce order level.

plainFields.name: carrier
plainFields.description: [Carrier] - The delivery company/provider name. Optional; can be null if ship-from-store or digital.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: [Tracking Number] - Carrier-provided shipment code for customer tracking.

plainFields.name: shipping_status
plainFields.description: [Shipping Status] - Current status of shipment independent of order status (e.g., pending, shipped, delivered, returned, etc.).

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: [Shipped Timestamp] - When the package was handed to carrier.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: [Delivered Timestamp] - When shipment confirmed delivered.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created] - When shipment record entered system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Last Update] - When shipping info last modified by system, admin, or carrier sync.

plainIndexes.name: idx_shipment_order_carrier
plainIndexes.description: Speeds carrier-based shipment queries, analytics, or API sync flows.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_return_request
models.description:
[Return Request Purpose] - Implements the customer-initiated return/cancellation workflow per compliance regulation and e-commerce expectation.

Each record represents a distinct request for either return or cancellation, with reference to order and customer, including reason, status, and timestamps. 3NF is enforced by isolating request data from main order rows, preventing transitive duplications.

Key relationships: ai_ecommerce_order, customer; target item(s) by order_item_id if required in extensions. Special behaviors: Tracked separately from order; each return/cancel tracked atomically.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Return Request PK] - Unique per request, supports auditing of customer claims.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: [Order FK] - Identifies the target order for return/cancellation logic.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Customer FK] - Initiator of the request.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: [Request Status] - Tracks return approval, pending, denied, or completed state in atomic field.

plainFields.name: request_type
plainFields.description: [Request Type] - Identifies 'return', 'cancellation', or other request variant.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: [Reason] - Optional customer-provided explanation, can be null for 'no reason' selected.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created] - When customer made the request.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: [Last Updated] - Audit trail timestamp for each request update.

plainIndexes.name: idx_return_order_status
plainIndexes.description: Speeds workflow for pending/processing requests per order.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_coupon
models.description:
Coupon entity - Implements the 'Discount System' and 'Coupon Issuance/Usage' requirements from 08_ai_ecommerce_discount_loyalty_payment.md.

Represents platform- or seller-issued coupons distributed to customers for redemption. Fully normalized: only core coupon data, no calculated aggregates or usage counts (these are in materialized views). For example, enables application of seller promotions and supports eligibility checks, referencing customers, sellers, and rules.

Key relationships: References issuing seller, owning customer, and related discount rule. Special behaviors: Enforces single/multi-use logic via unique index on (code, customer_id).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Each coupon is uniquely addressable.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Customer ownership] - Links coupon to intended customer, for personalized coupons. Nullable for platform-wide distribution.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: [Issuing seller] - Seller that issued this coupon. Nullable for platform coupons.

foreignFields.name: discount_rule_id
foreignFields.description: [Discount rule linkage] - Connects coupon with its discount definition logic.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description:
[Coupon code] - Unique identification used by customer at redemption.

Uniqueness enforced per customer/scope. E.g., SAVE10.

plainFields.name: issued_at
plainFields.description: [Issued timestamp] - When coupon was issued.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: [Expiration] - When coupon is no longer valid.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: [Active flag] - Whether coupon is available for redemption.

plainFields.name: usage_limit
plainFields.description: [Usage count limit] - How many times coupon can be redeemed.

plainFields.name: usage_per_customer_limit
plainFields.description: [Per-customer limit] - Max redemptions by single customer.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_loyalty_point
models.description:
Loyalty point record - Implements 'Loyalty Management: Reward/Spend' in 08_ai_ecommerce_discount_loyalty_payment.md.

Records loyalty point accrual or redemption event per customer. Strictly normalized: no running balance fields. Supports programmatic auditing and dispute resolution.

Key relationships: Linked to customer, order, and loyalty tier at event time. Special behavior: No aggregate/snapshot data here; belongs in MVs.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique for each point transaction.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Customer] - The customer for this transaction.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: [Order linkage] - Order involved in this point event, nullable.

foreignFields.name: loyalty_tier_id
foreignFields.description: [Tier at event] - The tier of the customer at the time of event.

plainFields.name: change_amount
plainFields.description: [Point change] - Points added or subtracted by this event.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: [Reason] - Explains why points were credited/debited (e.g., 'purchase').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Timestamp] - When event occurred.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_loyalty_tier
models.description:
Loyalty tier definition - Implements 'Loyalty/Points Tiering' from 08_ai_ecommerce_discount_loyalty_payment.md.

Normalized definition for each loyalty tier (e.g., Silver/Gold), with requirements, multipliers, and display order.

Key relationships: Referenced by loyalty points. Not per-user tier state (belongs on user record).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Each tier definition is unique.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: [Tier name] - e.g., Silver, Gold, Diamond.

plainFields.name: min_points_required
plainFields.description: [Minimum points] - Needed for tier attainment.

plainFields.name: multiplier
plainFields.description: [Point multiplier] - Earning/rate for this tier.

plainFields.name: sort_order
plainFields.description: [Sort order] - Controls tier sorting for display.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_wallet
models.description:
Customer wallet - Fulfills 'Deposit/Wallet Recharge' from 08_ai_ecommerce_discount_loyalty_payment.md.

Maintains customer wallet account for platform credits. Strictly normalized: only account metadata, no running balance here.

Key relationships: Linked to customer, used as ref in wallet_transaction. No cached balance values.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique wallet per customer/currency.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Customer ownership] - Each wallet linked to one customer/currency tuple.

plainFields.name: currency_code
plainFields.description: [Wallet currency] - ISO currency code.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created timestamp] - When wallet was opened.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: [Wallet status] - True if available for use.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_wallet_transaction
models.description:
Wallet transaction record - Implements 'Deposit/Spend/Refund' from 08_ai_ecommerce_discount_loyalty_payment.md.

Each record documents a wallet inflow/outflow; strictly normalized with no pre-calculated/cached balances. Enables full, auditable history for customer and compliance.

Key relationships: Linked to wallet, optionally to order/payment. All types: deposit/payment/refund/etc.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique per wallet transaction.

foreignFields.name: wallet_id
foreignFields.description: [Wallet] - Wallet owning this transaction.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: [Order linkage] - Related order if available.

foreignFields.name: payment_id
foreignFields.description: [Payment linkage] - Payment event if available.

plainFields.name: change_amount
plainFields.description: [Amount changed] - Money credited or debited for this transaction.

plainFields.name: currency_code
plainFields.description: [Currency] - ISO 4217 code.

plainFields.name: transaction_type
plainFields.description: [Type] - e.g., 'deposit', 'payment', 'refund', etc.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Timestamp] - When transaction occurred.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_payment_integration
models.description:
Payment integration definition - Realizes 'Multi-Method Payment' and 'Payment Integration Management' in 08_ai_ecommerce_discount_loyalty_payment.md.

Definition for payment gateways, wallets, and partner integrations. Contains configuration only; no runtime transactional data.

Key relationships: Referenced by payments and orders.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique integration config.

plainFields.name: provider_name
plainFields.description: [Provider] - E.g., Stripe, KCP, KakaoPay.

plainFields.name: configuration_json
plainFields.description: [Config blob] - Stores JSON settings and encrypted keys.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: [Status] - Whether this integration is available.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Timestamp] - When configured/updated.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_discount_rule
models.description:
Discount rule definition - Implements all coupon, loyalty, and promotional rules per 08_ai_ecommerce_discount_loyalty_payment.md.

Stores normalized discount logic for coupons/promotions. No calculated/per-customer data here; only definitions. Key relationships: referenced by coupons, referenced by campaigns. Special behaviors: Extensible rule engine via type+predicate.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique rule definition.

plainFields.name: rule_type
plainFields.description: [Type] - E.g., 'fixed_amount', 'percentage', 'stacking', etc.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: [Description] - Human-readable summary of the rule.

plainFields.name: predicate_json
plainFields.description: [Predicate/settings blob] - JSON describing eligibility and constraints.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created at] - Rule last revised.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_favorite
models.description: [Favorite Products Entity] - Implements the 'Favorites System' from personalization requirements. Allows customers to mark products as favorites. Maintains strict 3NF by modeling only atomic relationships—customer, product, tag. No derived or aggregated fields. Example use: when a user adds a favorite product for later quick access. Key relationships: references ai_ecommerce_customer, ai_ecommerce_product, and optionally ai_ecommerce_favorite_tag. Special: per-customer per-product favorite must be unique.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique system-generated UUID for this favorite entry. Non-derivable and guarantees row uniqueness.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Customer Reference] - References the customer that owns this favorite. Satisfies atomic link requirement. Example: a user favorites a product.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: [Product Reference] - References the product marked as favorite. Strictly one product per favorite. Example: a customer favorites a specific product.

foreignFields.name: favorite_tag_id
foreignFields.description: [Favorite Tag Reference] - Optionally references a tag to categorize this favorite. 3NF-compliant, tags separated from favorite entry. Example: grouping favorites under 'Gift Ideas' tag.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - Timestamp when the favorite was created. Immutable audit field.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_favorite_tag
models.description: [Favorite Tag Entity] - Implements 'Tagging & Organization' from personalization requirements. Lets customers group favorites by tag. Maintains 3NF by storing only tag name/ownership. Example: tags like 'Wishlist', 'Gift', 'To Buy'. Key relation: links to ai_ecommerce_customer; tag name unique per-customer.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique UUID for user tag. Required for tag referencing in favorites.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Tag Owner Reference] - Points to the customer who owns this tag. Each customer can name tags independently.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: [Tag Name] - The customer-defined label for this grouping. Strictly unique per customer. Example: 'For Mom'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Created Timestamp] - When the tag was created first. Auditable and 3NF-compliant.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_recommendation
models.description: [Personalized Recommendation Entity] - Implements 'Personalized Recommendations' from the requirements. Stores system-generated recommendations for a user and product, no derived or computed data. Maintains atomic links to customer, recommended product, optional snapshot. For example: logging a daily AI suggestion for a product. Special: one record per customer-product-timestamp, 3NF. References ai_ecommerce_customer, ai_ecommerce_product, ai_ecommerce_snapshot.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique identifier for this recommendation entry.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Recommendation recipient] - The customer that gets this recommendation.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: [Recommended product] - The product being recommended for this user.

foreignFields.name: snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: [Recommendation context snapshot] - Links to personalization snapshot that informed this recommendation, if present.

plainFields.name: recommended_at
plainFields.description: [Recommended Timestamp] - When the recommendation was created by the system.

plainFields.name: reason_code
plainFields.description: [Reason Code] - AI-generated string indicating why this was recommended (e.g., 'similar_items'). Null for standard recommendations.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_snapshot
models.description: [Personalization Snapshot Entity] - Implements 'Snapshotting & Portability'. Records a user's personalization state snapshot. Only atomic properties captured, no aggregates. Used for restoring preferences/favorites (cross-device). Key: references ai_ecommerce_customer. Example: periodic backup or device sync snapshot.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique snapshot event id.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Customer Reference] - Who this snapshot is for.

plainFields.name: snapshot_type
plainFields.description: [Snapshot Type] - Describes captured data, e.g. 'favorites', 'settings', 'tags'.

plainFields.name: taken_at
plainFields.description: [Taken Timestamp] - When the snapshot was taken.

plainFields.name: blob_uri
plainFields.description: [Blob Storage URI] - Location (usually cloud URI) of the full snapshot data.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_personalization_config
models.description: [Personalization Config Entity] - Implements admin/user-level personalization system parameters. Only atomic config keys, never status or results. Example: AI model version, tuning parameter. Key relationships: ai_ecommerce_administrator (who set), customer optional. Maintains strict 3NF (config_key/value pairs, not aggregates).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique system-generated id for this config row.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: [Admin Reference] - Who set/applied this config.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Customer Reference] - Optionally, per-user config. Null if global/system config.

plainFields.name: config_key
plainFields.description: [Config Key] - Name specifying which setting is being applied.

plainFields.name: config_value
plainFields.description: [Config Value] - Value associated with config key, usually string or URI.

plainFields.name: applied_at
plainFields.description: [Applied Timestamp] - When config went into effect.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_personalization_analytics
models.description: [Personalization Analytics Entity] - Implements atomic logging of personalization/favorite/recommendation engagement for analytics, never aggregates. For meaningful reporting/audits. Links: ai_ecommerce_customer (actor), ai_ecommerce_administrator (optional analyzer), ai_ecommerce_product (for event context). Usage: logging clicks, adding/removing favorite, etc. Strict 3NF, one row per action/event.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary key] - Unique analytics event id (UUID).

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: [Customer Reference] - Who triggered event.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: [Admin Reference] - Optional administrator involved in analytics/audit.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: [Product Reference] - Contextual product attached to the event.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: [Event Type] - e.g., 'favorite_add', 'favorite_remove', 'rec_click'.

plainFields.name: event_at
plainFields.description: [Event Occurrence] - When analytics event happened.

plainFields.name: details_json
plainFields.description: [Details JSON] - Arbitrary serialized JSON for extensible event data.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_audit_logs
models.description:
[Platform Audit Log] - This implements platform-wide audit requirements from the compliance and system documentation. 

The purpose of this model is to capture all major user/system actions across the platform for traceability and legal/audit purposes. Maintains 3NF by only recording atomic events; all aggregates must be computed externally. Example: Storing each API call, role change, data update. 

Key relationships: related to users (customer, seller, admin) via polymorphic actor fields, and can reference event objects by foreign keys. Special behaviors: Immutable records, soft deletion for audit compliance.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description:
[Primary Key] - Implements unique identifier requirement.
A UUID uniquely identifies each audit record, providing a tamper-proof anchor for traceability.

foreignFields.name: actor_customer_id
foreignFields.description:
[Polymorphic Actor Customer FK] - Implements actor auditing for customers.
Links the log entry to the customer entity if the action was taken by a customer. Maintains normalization by referencing only the actor’s id, not repeating user data.
Optional; null unless the action came from a customer.

foreignFields.name: actor_seller_id
foreignFields.description:
[Polymorphic Actor Seller FK] - Implements actor auditing for sellers.
Links the action to a seller when relevant, preserving entity relationships without redundancy.
Nullable for non-seller actions.
Maintains normalized linkage.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_id
foreignFields.description:
[Polymorphic Actor Admin FK] - Implements admin action source traceability.
Enforces role-based normalization by relating each admin action to the admin entity without duplicating data.
Nullable when not an admin action.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description:
[Action Type] - Implements action type requirement.
Atomic indicator of the type of event ("login", "update_order", etc.)
Remains normalized as a primitive value for query/aggregation.

plainFields.name: target_table
plainFields.description:
[Target Table] - Implements audit context requirement.
Identifies which business table/entity is affected (e.g., "ai_ecommerce_order"). Ensures normalization; does not store denormalized object state.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description:
[Target Entity FK] - Implements object-focused audit linking.
Stores the UUID of the affected entity. Used for join/audit search.
Remains atomic, normalized.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
[Description/Details] - Implements detailed audit record context.
Stores a brief, atomic note about the audit event. Example: "Order cancelled by admin." Purely descriptive.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
[Creation Timestamp] - Implements temporal logging requirement.
Record of when the event occurred. Required for compliance and audit sequencing.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: [Soft Delete Timestamp] - Soft-deletion audit field, enables logical removal while maintaining audit trail. Stays null if active.

plainIndexes.description: [Index pattern] For querying logs by customer and time.
[Index pattern] For querying logs by seller and time.
[Index pattern] For querying logs by admin and time.

ginIndexes.description: [Full-text search] Enables fast text search over audit log descriptions.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_system_events
models.description:
[System Events] - This implements system-level event tracking from the architecture and event orchestration requirements.

Used to persist domain and integration events (e.g., "order_created", "payment_captured") supporting event-driven design, compliance, debug traceability. 3NF is maintained—no aggregates or blobs; only atomic event info is captured. Example: recording "review_posted" event for async processing.

Key relationships: Possible link to orders/products/users by target_id; system event logs can be externally correlated with business tables. Special behaviors: Append-only, never updated/deleted except for rare compliance removal.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Unique event record identifier implementing append-only event log design.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: [Event Type] - Implements event kind, e.g., "order_created". Atomic, normalized.

plainFields.name: target_table
plainFields.description: [Target Table] - Table/entity impacted by event; for cross-domain analytics without denormalization.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: [Target ID] - UUID of affected row/entity. Maintains joinability.

plainFields.name: payload_json
plainFields.description: [Event Payload] - JSON-encoded atomic event payload. Maintains normalization by not embedding related rows; only the raw event data.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Event Created] - Timestamp for event append log.

plainIndexes.description: [Event query pattern] For filtering by event type and recency.

ginIndexes.description: [GIN for search] For advanced event payload search/fuzzy matching.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_compliance_audits
models.description:
[Compliance Audit Record] - Implements regulatory compliance logging and audit rule enforcement from the compliance documentation.

Captures all compliance-relevant events (policy updates, privacy requests, financial reviews) for legal defensibility. Maintains strict normalization: all compliance actions atomic, no pre-computed summaries.
Example: capturing "GDPR erase request", "PCI review", etc.

Key relationships: May reference administrators or user actions by foreign key. Special behaviors: (1) Tamper-evident, (2) direct role-to-event mapping.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Compliance audit record UUID.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description:
[Administrator FK] - Admin responsible for compliance action.
Links to administrator (if available) for actor tracking. Maintains normalized responsibility representation.

plainFields.name: audit_type
plainFields.description: [Audit Type] - E.g., "GDPR_Delete", "PCI_Review". Atomic. Normalized for query.

plainFields.name: subject_table
plainFields.description: [Subject Table] - Table/entity under compliance audit. Simple string, not a denormalized blob or join.

plainFields.name: subject_id
plainFields.description: [Subject ID] - Affected entity row UUID. Normalized linkage.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: [Status] - Status value (e.g., "pending", "approved", "rejected"). Maintains normalization by single value per event.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: [Notes/Context] - Atomic audit context. Purely descriptive.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: [Audit Created] - When the compliance event occurred.

uniqueIndexes.description: [Unique per subject/type] Prevents duplicate compliance audit logs for the same action.

plainIndexes.description: [Querying compliance actions by admin and time].

ginIndexes.description: [GIN search] Fast lookup by note content.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_mv_daily_stats
models.description:
[Daily Statistics - Materialized View] - Implements denormalized, pre-computed daily platform statistics for reporting/performance from architecture requirements.

Caches day-level aggregates (total orders, revenue, logins, etc.) for analytics dashboards. Normalization is intentionally relaxed (denormalization allowed) for read efficiency; raw detail persists in normalized tables. Example: reporting yesterday’s sales/orders across platform.

Key relationships: Read-only view; not updated directly. Special behaviors: auto-refresh, never modified by app logic, aggregates by date.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: [Primary Key] - Row identifier for aggregation row.

plainFields.name: stat_date
plainFields.description: [Statistic Date] - Date of the statistics (ISO date stored as string).

plainFields.name: order_count
plainFields.description: [Order Count] - Number of orders on this date. Denormalized aggregation.

plainFields.name: revenue_amount
plainFields.description: [Revenue Amount] - Total sales in double on that date. Denormalized.

plainFields.name: login_count
plainFields.description: [Login Count] - Number of unique account logins that day. Denormalized.

plainFields.name: signups_count
plainFields.description: [Signups Count] - Total user signups. Denormalized.

plainFields.name: review_count
plainFields.description: [Review Count] - Number of new reviews. Denormalized.

uniqueIndexes.description: [Unique per date] Ensures one row per date.

models.name: ai_ecommerce_mv_trending_products
models.description:
[Trending Products - Materialized View] - Implements denormalized, pre-computed trending product statistics from analytics and AI documentation.

Tracks high-performing products by day/week/month for recommendation, featuring, and dashboards. Normalization is relaxed; aggregates like rank, counts, and composite scores are pre-computed here. Example: Populating “Trending Now” on homepage.

Key relationships: Links to product entity by foreign key; not written by app logic. Special behaviors: refreshed/cached, used for automated scripts or admin apps.

### `ai_ecommerce_customers`

[Customer Identity & Access] - Implements registration/authentication and Customer Role requirements from 03_ai_ecommerce_user_management.md. Each instance represents a person with customer capabilities (browsing, buying, reviewing, profile management). Enforces 3NF by linking to unique user profile and not duplicating profile/address info. Key relationships: ai_ecommerce_user_profiles (mandatory 1:1), ai_ecommerce_user_addresses (1:N), ai_ecommerce_user_oauth (1:N), ai_ecommerce_user_audit_logs (1:N). Behavioral notes: supports soft-deletion and unique email/oauth identity via related tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Primary Key] - Implements unique row identity; referenced throughout system. Immutable and atomic for all customer records.
- `profile_id`: [User Profile Relation] - 1:1 relation to ai_ecommerce_user_profiles; strictly normalized; unique required FK.
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - For audit and traceability.
- `updated_at`: [Last Updated Timestamp] - For compliance tracking.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft Delete] - If set, account is deactivated but retained for compliance; null if active.

### `ai_ecommerce_sellers`

[Seller Identity & Onboarding] - Fulfills seller onboarding, authentication, and identity requirements in 04_ai_ecommerce_seller_admin_management.md. Each record is a business account with seller privileges, strictly normalized with profile linkage. Key relationships: ai_ecommerce_user_profiles (mandatory 1:1), ai_ecommerce_user_addresses (1:N), ai_ecommerce_user_oauth (1:N), ai_ecommerce_user_audit_logs (1:N). Seller approval states handled in dedicated onboarding tables. Not duplicated across profiles. Behavioral notes: soft-delete for business user deactivation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Primary Key] - Unique seller identity for business account; referenced in all seller business flows.
- `profile_id`: [User Profile Relation] - 1:1 relation to ai_ecommerce_user_profiles; unique required FK.
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - For audit/compliance.
- `updated_at`: [Last Updated Timestamp] - Tracks changes/audits.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft Delete] - Set if seller account is inactive (audit/compl.), null if active.

### `ai_ecommerce_administrators`

[Administrator Identity] - Implements admin role/account separation (03_ai_ecommerce_user_management.md, 04_ai_ecommerce_seller_admin_management.md). Only platform admins—distinct from sellers/customers. Strictly normalized: one profile per admin. Key relationships: ai_ecommerce_user_profiles (mandatory 1:1), ai_ecommerce_user_audit_logs (1:N). Use: Action/audit log linkage, privilege separation. Notes: Only admin-privileged users reside here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Primary Key] - Unique admin identity; referenced in admin/audit flows.
- `profile_id`: [User Profile Relation] - 1:1 relation to ai_ecommerce_user_profiles; unique per admin.
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - Created for traceability.
- `updated_at`: [Last Updated Timestamp] - Compliance/audit edits.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft Delete] - Admin deactivation timestamp; null if active.

### `ai_ecommerce_user_profiles`

[User Profile] - Implements core profile for customer, seller, admin per 03_ai_ecommerce_user_management.md & 04_ai_ecommerce_seller_admin_management.md, with display, comms, and privacy settings. Strict 3NF: never duplicated (referenced by all identity tables). Central for self-service updates, comms config, and unique email identity. Behavioral notes: flexible optional fields, system-wide email uniqueness enforced here. Key relationships: referenced everywhere user profile needed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Primary Key] - One-to-one with every user/seller/admin identity.
- `nickname`: [Display Nickname] - User-facing display name (not unique).
- `avatar_uri`: [Profile Image] - Optional (avatar or profile photo).
- `email`: [Email Address] - System-wide unique (communication & login).
- `phone_number`: [Phone Number] - Optionally supplied for comms channels/MFA.
- `communication_consent`: [Communication Consent] - Explicit opt-in for platform messaging.
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - Compliance/audit trails.
- `updated_at`: [Updated Timestamp] - Last profile update.

### `ai_ecommerce_user_addresses`

[User Addresses] - Implements normalized delivery/billing/multi-address per 03_ai_ecommerce_user_management.md. 1:N with ai_ecommerce_user_profiles (profile_id FK). Flexible for domestic/international. Not repeated in parent. Behavioral: Soft delete for audit, region validation handled elsewhere. Examples: Used at checkout/order, customer address book.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Primary Key] - Unique address, referenced by fulfillment etc.
- `profile_id`: [Profile FK] - Owner of address; 1:N relationship from profile.
- `address_type`: [Address Type] - 'default', 'billing', or 'delivery'; logical separation.
- `name`: [Recipient Name] - Who will receive item at this address.
- `phone_number`: [Recipient Phone] - Delivery contact number.
- `postal_code`: [Postal Code] - Delivery area postal code (FMS, INTL OK).
- `address_line1`: [Main Address Line] - Street/road/building etc.
- `address_line2`: [Secondary Address Line] - Apartment/unit/floor, optional.
- `custom_label`: [Custom Label] - User-supplied e.g. 'Work', 'Mom's house'.
- `region_code`: [Region/Country Code] - ISO/country/region/locale code as required.
- `is_default`: [Default Address] - True if active default; service enforced.
- `created_at`: [Created Timestamp] - Record creation date/time.
- `updated_at`: [Last Edited Timestamp] - Compliance/audit trail.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft Delete] - Timestamp of soft delete/null if active.

[User OAuth Account] - Fulfills single/external sign-on per 03_ai_ecommerce_user_management.md. 1:N for providers per user profile. Model is normalized, each record one provider-user pair. Key: Uniqueness by provider+provider_user_id. Used for federated identity/login/account linking, never for regular credential storage. Behavioral: unique composite PK for anti-duplication.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Primary Key] - Unique for OAuth account association/audit.
- `profile_id`: [Profile FK] - Links OAuth to user's profile (1:N).
- `provider`: [Auth Provider] - e.g. 'google', 'apple', 'kakao', etc.
- `provider_user_id`: [Provider User ID] - Unique in provider namespace.
- `created_at`: [Binding Created] - When account linkage made/audited.

### `ai_ecommerce_user_audit_logs`

[User Audit Log] - Implements sensitive action/trace requirements in 03_ai_ecommerce_user_management.md; logs changes, logins, security events. 3NF-compliant: all actionable events in this log, never duplicated in main profile tables. Behavioral: Write-once/append-only (no delete allowed), event code/JSON in payload, links to acting user profile. Typical: Tracks login, registration, reset, account changes, compliance events.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Primary Key] - One-to-each audit event; globally unique.
- `profile_id`: [Profile FK] - Traces event actor.
- `event_type`: [Audit Event Type] - 'registration', 'login', 'profile_update', etc. Coded by API/service.
- `event_payload`: [Payload] - Opaque log info/context (e.g. IP, device, JSON payload).
- `created_at`: [Log Created] - Exact time event happened.

Enables individuals to act as customers—browsing, ordering, reviewing—through a normalized identity linked 1:1 with user profile for account management. Strict 3NF ensures profile/address/oauth are never duplicated here. For example, used as owner of a cart, order, or review.

### `ai_ecommerce_administrator`
